:::{#def-bias-variance-tradeoff}
#### Bias--variance trade-off

Let $g_1, \ldots, g_L$ be [fitting procedures](#def-fitting-procedure),
each [at least as flexible](#def-flexibility) as the one before,
and let $\trainset$ be a random [training set](#def-training-set).
At a covariate value $x$,
there is a **bias--variance trade-off** among them
when, from each procedure to the next,
the squared [bias](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/variance-covariance.html#def-prediction-bias)
of the prediction does not rise
and its [variance](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/variance-covariance.html#def-variance)
does not fall:

$$
\ba
\sqf{\bias{g_{l+1}\paren{x; \trainset}}} &\le \sqf{\bias{g_l\paren{x; \trainset}}},
\\
\Var{g_{l+1}\paren{x; \trainset}} &\ge \Var{g_l\paren{x; \trainset}},
\qquad l = 1, \ldots, L - 1.
\ea
$$ {#eq-bias-variance-tradeoff}
